result.reason: Bounded unit repair requires contract revision

independent_findings.hypothesis: The frozen acceptance requirements conflict: PreparedAssetsAreInspectable requires a non-null private static TMP_FontAsset, while Story_NFR_02 forbids static declarations in lobby runtime sources. Story_NFR_03 requires marquee text exactly 'own-42', whereas US-L1-04 and Story_L1_04 require player-name-prefixed marquee content. Story_L1_05 requires Start to change the selected tier, but US-L9-05 requires it to begin matching at the selected tier. These acceptance contradictions require contract/test-owner reconciliation; implementing the existing runtime stubs alone cannot resolve them faithfully.

The declared behavior and ownership are sufficient. SHELL-owned LobbyShellBindings and ConfigureLobbyRehearsal remain no-ops, explaining missing navigation, bindings and Root acquisition; these prerequisite defects belong to SHELL, not an expansion of ECON ownership. Persisted account/card and reconciliation restoration failures belong to ECON. Route repairs to the existing owners and rerun integrated verification; the nonbehavioral receipt does not establish valid TDD evidence.

The supplied SHELL coordinator and ConfigureLobbyRehearsal are no-op stubs, explaining empty routes, missing bound views and ordinary-entry null references. These are missing prerequisite implementations owned by declared peer SHELL, not a contract gap or permission to expand MATCH ownership. Route repairs to the existing owners and verify the integrated candidate; the nonbehavioral evidence flag does not establish TDD or require weakening acceptance.

The supplied SHELL implementation is nonfunctional: EnterAsync/OpenAsync/BindView are no-ops, BoundViewCount is always zero, and ConfigureLobbyRehearsal does nothing. This explains missing navigation, controls and world-read transitions, while configured Monopoly entry falls into ordinary match preparation. These responsibilities and ownership are already explicit in the contract. Route prerequisite repairs to SHELL, not SOCIAL; preserve frozen tests and ownership. The nonbehavioral verification receipt does not establish behavioral TDD or successful integration.

The required entry and binding behavior is explicitly specified, but LobbyShellBindings.EnterAsync/OpenAsync/CommandAsync and Monopoly.ConfigureLobbyRehearsal are no-ops. This explains empty routes, missing bound controls and failure to reach the injected Root port. These prerequisite defects belong to SHELL, not RECORDS; existing ownership and dependency mappings already provide the repair route without changing the contract. Nonbehavioral verification evidence does not establish TDD success.
